name: henngelm/background-generator-javascript
description: Uses two HTML <input type='color'> pickers (yielding hex values like #ff0000) plus a 'Random Generator' button that generates random 24-bit hex colors using Math.random()*0xFFFFFF shifted to integer then converted to hex string. Defaults: green (#00ff00) to red (#ff0000). Applies selected colors as CSS linear-gradient on the body background.

name: MichaelRendon/Background-Generator
description: Pure manual color selection via two HTML <input type='color'> pickers. No random generation, no algorithmic selection. Default values: cyan (#11D8EE) and magenta (#FC03E9). User manually picks both gradient endpoints using the browser's native color picker widget. Results applied as CSS linear-gradient on body.

name: Refactoring UI
description: Commercial book/product by Adam Wathan & Steve Schoger (Tailwind CSS creators). Their documented color approach (from the public article 'Building Your Color Palette' at /previews/building-your-color-palette/) explicitly REJECTS algorithmic color palette generators. Instead prescribes a systematic but fully manual methodology: (1) Define 3 categories: Greys (8-10 shades for text/backgrounds/panels), Primary colors (1-2 with 5-10 shades each), Accent colors (multiple with 5-10 shades each). (2) Choose a base color (mid-range, suitable as button background). (3) Find edges manually by adjusting saturation and lightness - darkest shade for text, lightest for tinted backgrounds. (4) Fill gaps via divide-and-conquer: pick shade 700 (between darkest and base), shade 300 (between base and lightest), then fill 800, 600, 400, 200. Uses a 9-step numbering system (100-900, base at 500). Explicitly advises AGAINST automated CSS preprocessor functions like 'lighten'/'darken' for generating shades. Core philosophy: 'It's not a science - trust your eyes, not the numbers.'
key_principles: Define fixed shade sets upfront, not generated on-the-fly
Reject algorithmic palette generators (triad, major fourth, etc.)
Manual visual adjustment of saturation and lightness
Divide-and-conquer gap filling between darkest, base, and lightest
True black avoided in favor of dark grey
Semantic color categories: greys, primary, accent
No scientific/mathematical formula - trust eyes over numbers
